about: Weekend Stage curriculum: ten famous TED talks, one per weekend, easiest to hardest. Links, times and our own delivery notes only: never a transcript, never TED audio or video (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, see references/stage_design.md).

talks.title: Try something new for 30 days
talks.speaker: Matt Cutts
talks.subject: Habits
talks.move: One idea, short sentences, light personal evidence, a crisp close
watch_for: How short each sentence is, and how each one lands before the next starts
Where he lets a laugh happen instead of rushing past it
The close: one direct question to the room, then he stops

take_b.cares: a low-risk way to say yes
take_b.prompt: Pitch a 30-day pilot of an AI agent: what you will try, what you will measure, and what happens on day 31.

take_c.twist: The same pitch in 90 seconds. Cut, don't rush.

talks.title: How to introduce yourself — and get hired
talks.speaker: Rebecca Okamoto
talks.subject: Careers
talks.move: An introduction of 20 words or fewer, built so the listener asks for more; then silence
watch_for: The before-and-after story she opens with, told in under a minute
Each formula is said once, plainly, then shown with an example
The pause after each example introduction: she lets it land

segment.label: Where she lays out the introduction formulas

take_b.cares: what you can do for them, in one breath
take_b.prompt: Three introductions of 20 words or fewer: a Principal Engineer interview, a customer kickoff, an executive in a lift. Pause after each.

take_c.twist: They say: “Tell me more.” Give 30 seconds of detail on your best introduction, then stop and hold the silence.

talks.title: How to speak so that people want to listen
talks.speaker: Julian Treasure
talks.subject: Voice
talks.move: Deliberate shifts in register, pace, pitch and volume; silence as a tool
watch_for: He demonstrates each voice tool as he names it: listen for the change
How quiet he gets when he wants attention
His pace just before a key line, and just after it

take_b.cares: what the outage cost and whether it happens again
take_b.prompt: Explain an outage you handled with three planned voice shifts: slow down for the cost, drop your pitch for the fix, go quiet for the ask.

take_c.twist: Say it twice: first completely flat, one pitch and one pace; then with the full toolbox. Hear the difference.

talks.title: How great leaders inspire action
talks.speaker: Simon Sinek
talks.subject: Leadership
talks.move: Teach one simple model while drawing it; repeat the core line; stay unhurried
watch_for: He draws the model as he explains it, so the audience watches it grow
One core line comes back several times, in the same words each time
A calm, conversational pace, even at the biggest claims

take_b.cares: why this change, before what it costs
take_b.prompt: Your architecture recommendation, starting with why. Draw it on paper, on camera, as you go.

take_c.twist: No notes and no paper: the same recommendation in 2 minutes, the model drawn in the air.

talks.title: The puzzle of motivation
talks.speaker: Dan Pink
talks.subject: Business science
talks.move: Argue like a lawyer: claim, evidence, pause, conclusion
watch_for: He frames the talk as a case put to a jury, and keeps that frame
Each piece of evidence gets a short pause before the conclusion
Humour about himself early buys trust for the hard claim later

take_b.prompt: Make the case for evals before scale: one claim, three pieces of evidence, one conclusion.

take_c.twist: They interrupt: “What's the biggest risk?” Answer one level deeper, then stop.

talks.title: The best stats you've ever seen
talks.speaker: Hans Rosling
talks.subject: Data and global health
talks.move: Narrate data like live sport: point, build suspense, react to the numbers
watch_for: He tells you where to look before the data moves
His energy rises with the chart: he reacts like a commentator
Each chart ends on one plain sentence about what it means

take_b.cares: what the numbers mean for next quarter
take_b.prompt: Narrate a real chart from your work (eval results, a dashboard): where to look, what moved, what it means.

take_c.twist: The 60-second exec version: the headline number first, one reason, one ask.

talks.title: Do schools kill creativity?
talks.speaker: Sir Ken Robinson
talks.subject: Education
talks.move: Comic timing: understatement, and the pause before and after the laugh
watch_for: How flat his voice stays on the funny lines
The pause he leaves for the laugh, and how he waits it out
Asides that sound unplanned but land every time

take_b.cares: whether today will be worth their time
take_b.prompt: Open a customer workshop with a light, true story about a deployment that went wrong, and what it taught you.

take_c.twist: Cold open: no warm-up and no notes. The first take counts.

talks.title: The power of vulnerability
talks.speaker: Brené Brown
talks.subject: Psychology
talks.move: Turn from research to a personal admission, and slow down at the turn
watch_for: Humour about herself early lowers the room's guard
Where she slows down: the moment the research becomes personal
She names an uncomfortable feeling plainly instead of explaining it away

segment.label: The turn from research to her own story

take_b.cares: self-awareness, not a polished success story
take_b.prompt: Tell me about a mistake you made as an architect: what happened, what you felt, what you changed.

take_c.twist: The same story with no notes, in one take. If you stumble, keep going.

talks.title: The danger of a single story
talks.speaker: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
talks.subject: Literature and culture
talks.move: Calm, warm storytelling with concrete detail; land the point quietly
watch_for: Small, concrete details carry each story, not adjectives
She almost never raises her voice, and the room leans in
The big point arrives quietly, after the stories have earned it

take_b.cares: how you judge people and situations
take_b.prompt: A customer story where your first read of a stakeholder was wrong: the detail that changed your mind.

take_c.twist: Seated, at half volume: presence without energy tricks.

talks.title: We need to talk about an injustice
talks.speaker: Bryan Stevenson
talks.subject: Justice
talks.move: Gravitas: low pitch, slow pace, long pauses; persuade without pushing
watch_for: Stories come first; the argument arrives only after them
Low, steady pitch and long pauses, even at the strongest moments
He never raises his voice to make a hard point

take_b.prompt: Capstone: a 5-minute talk on your own idea for FDE work, using moves from weeks 1 to 9.

take_c.twist: Encore: your capstone's first minute again, standing, no notes, one take. Then watch week 1 beside it.
